entities.name: Columbia Records
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Columbia Records, founded in 1887 as the Columbia Phonograph Company — making it one of the oldest recorded music companies in existence, predating the sound recording industry's commercial foundations — is one of the most historically significant and commercially successful record labels ever established, responsible for pioneering the development of the LP (long-playing record) in 1948, and home to Miles Davis, Bob Dylan, Billie Holiday, Johnny Cash, Bruce Springsteen, Beyoncé, and hundreds of other defining artists across every genre and era.

Columbia's early history is intertwined with the very foundations of the recorded music industry: it was one of the first companies to commercially exploit Edison's phonograph technology, competing with Victor (later RCA Victor) for the infant market. Columbia's most technically significant contribution was the invention of the LP by Peter Goldmark in 1948 — the 33⅓ RPM long-playing vinyl record that replaced the 78 RPM shellac disc, enabling continuous music for 22+ minutes per side and transforming how music was organized, sold, and experienced by listeners worldwide.

Columbia Records' artistic legacy is incomparable: Miles Davis's decade-long relationship produced Kind of Blue (1959, the best-selling jazz album of all time), Bitches Brew (1970, defining jazz fusion), and multiple other masterpieces. Bob Dylan signed with Columbia in 1961 and made the label the home of the folk-rock revolution. Johnny Cash recorded at Columbia from 1958-1986. Beyoncé, Bruce Springsteen, Adele, and contemporary superstars have continued the tradition. Now part of Sony Music Entertainment, Columbia maintains its status as one of the music industry's most prestigious labels.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Columbia Records — the oldest major label (1887), inventor of the LP format (1948), home to Miles Davis's Kind of Blue, Bob Dylan's revolution, Johnny Cash, and Beyoncé — is the most historically continuous and arguably most significant record label in the history of recorded music.
